extraction.name: Evaluating Object Hallucination in Large Vision-Language Models
extraction.description: This paper presents a systematic study on object hallucination of large vision-language models (LVLMs).
extraction.creator: Yifan Li, Yifan Du, Kun Zhou, Jinpeng Wang, Wayne Xin Zhao, Ji-Rong Wen
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset used in this study is MSCOCO, a large-scale image recognition, segmentation, and captioning dataset.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The LVLMs were fine-tuned on visual instruction data, which was generated based on the MSCOCO dataset.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The analysis of object hallucination was conducted using the CHAIR metric and a proposed polling-based object probing evaluation (POPE) method.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The object hallucination issue in LVLMs can have a significant impact on their performance in real-world applications, particularly in safety-critical scenarios such as autonomous driving.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: LVLMs tend to hallucinate objects that frequently appear or co-occur in the visual instruction dataset.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The existing evaluation methods for object hallucination in LVLMs are sensitive to input instructions and require object annotations and manually designed rules for evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset and evaluation methods proposed in this study can be used for evaluating object hallucination in LVLMs and improving their reliability and human alignment.
